No one warned her.
Chamoli, Uttarakhand, 7 February 2021

The flood took 20–30 minutes to reach the people downstream.

That was enough time to run.

No warning came.

200+ dead or missing
The world made a promise

Every person on Earth, warned in time.

fewer disaster deaths where warnings are strong
UN Early Warnings for All, UNDRR & WMO, Global Status of MHEWS 2025

But warnings travel on networks
that break first.

India already writes the warnings. 134 billion sent so far.

Every one of them travels the same road: the mobile network.

Dharali, August 2025. The flood took the towers first.

Jammu and Kashmir, August 2025. Fibre was cut, and phones went silent for a day.

And 8,985 Indian villages have no mobile tower at all.

We set out to change that.

Where we start

Chamoli and Pithoragarh hold Uttarakhand's five most dangerous glacial lakes.

The State is putting sensors on them. MARK makes sure their warning reaches the village.
